items.subject: The commit-msg store-citation hook resolves memory in only one of the two stores and refuses from 2026-09-25
evidence: ops/store_citation.py:66 (at 6079095f5) resolved memory:<name> and [[<name>]] against ~/.claude/projects/C--Codex-ThriftyCrew/memory only

measured 2026-09-22 15:10: ~/.claude/projects/C--Codex/memory holds 199 memos and C--Codex-ThriftyCrew/memory 187; ps51-bomless-read-is-cp1252.md exists in C--Codex and is ABSENT from C--Codex-ThriftyCrew; no other projects/*/memory directory holds more than 5 files
REFUSE_FROM = 2026-09-25 in the same file: from that date an unresolvable citation refuses the commit
items.root_cause: Claude Code keys a session's memory directory on the directory it was launched from, so the estate has two live memory stores, and the resolver held one hard-coded path that is right only for sessions launched in C:\Codex\ThriftyCrew (F1: one fact, 'where the memory store is', held in one place that is wrong for half the sessions). The failure is selective: a memo that happens to exist in both stores resolves, so it looked like it worked.

root_fix.what: the list of memory stores lives in one named constant and every memory lookup goes through one function that walks it
root_fix.exact_change: MEMORY_PROJECTS = ("C--Codex-ThriftyCrew", "C--Codex") with a comment saying why there are two and that a third launch root is added there; home_store() returns memories = every store's path (memory keeps the first for compatibility); memory_dirs(store) returns that list; resolve() checks a memory: or [[ ]] citation against every store and the bare-path branch walks skills, its parent, then every memory store

blast_radius.measured_by: directory listing of both stores on 2026-09-22 15:10
names: every memo in C--Codex/memory, e.g. ps51-bomless-read-is-cp1252
blast_radius.risk: a citation now resolves if it exists in EITHER store; a citation in neither is still refused (fixtured)

proof.clean_twin: with both stores listed, a memo held only by the second resolves in both spellings (memory: and [[ ]]), a memo in the first still resolves, and home_store() lists C--Codex-ThriftyCrew then C--Codex

items.subject: verify-bulk-edit's line-ending invariant has no production call site
evidence: ops/verify-bulk-edit.ps1 at 6079095f5: Test-EolUnchanged is defined at line 97 and called only from its own -SelfTest (two cases); the live path never calls it
ops/hooks/pre-commit refusal text advertises 'BOM state, line-ending style, a clean parse, or a call to a function the file cannot resolve'

git ls-files --eol on 2026-09-22 15:20: 8,884 i/lf, 39 i/-text, 333 i/none, 0 i/crlf, 0 i/mixed; .gitattributes has text=auto eol=lf since 2026-09-06, so git normalises every text file to LF in the index
items.root_cause: the invariant was written as a comparison of working-file text against HEAD, which cannot be run honestly (git normalises line endings, so a working CRLF file against an LF blob is not a flip: the 2026-09-05 false positive), so it was fixtured and never wired, and the hook's text kept advertising it (F4: a check that never looks reads the same as one that found nothing)

root_fix.what: the line-ending invariant reads what the commit will actually STORE: the index eol of each staged path, from git's own census, where a text blob that is not LF is the finding
root_fix.exact_change: replace Test-EolUnchanged with Get-IndexEolFindings, a pure function over 'git ls-files --eol' lines that returns a finding for any i/crlf or i/mixed entry (i/lf, i/-text, i/none are clean); the live -Staged path runs git ls-files --eol over the staged names and adds 'EOL           <path> - stored <i/..>' findings; the summary line prints the eol-checked count; the working-tree mode says the eol check is staged-only

blast_radius.measured_as: tracked text files stored with a non-LF blob
blast_radius.risk: a file marked -text (binary) must never be judged: i/-text is clean by construction and fixtured

proof.must_fire_case: frozen git ls-files --eol lines: 'i/crlf w/crlf attr/-text     x.ps1' and 'i/mixed w/mixed attr/                 y.txt' each produce one EOL finding naming the path
proof.clean_twin: 'i/lf w/crlf attr/text=auto eol=lf  z.ps1' (the 2026-09-05 working-copy CRLF over an LF blob) produces none, and a binary 'i/-text w/-text attr/-text a.png' and an empty 'i/none w/none attr/text=auto eol=lf e.txt' produce none; the live path over a staged LF file reports eol_checked=1 and no finding

Proof: -SelfTest exit 0 (4 new EOL cases); live -Staged run printed eol_checked=1, 0 findings; a throwaway repo with a -text CRLF blob fed real git ls-files --eol output and the function named exactly that path.
items.premise_verified: true: grep over ops/verify-bulk-edit.ps1 found Test-EolUnchanged only at its definition and two self-test cases; git ls-files --eol read 8,884 i/lf and 0 i/crlf
